message.content:
The three major schisms that have shaped Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Dates | Key Outcomes |
|---|--------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism of 1054** (East–West Schism) | 1054 CE | Formal split between the Roman Catholic Church (West) and the Eastern Orthodox Church (East). |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** (leading to Lutheranism, Reformed, Anglican) | 1517 – 1648 CE | Break from the Roman Catholic Church, giving rise to Lutheranism, Calvinism, Anglicanism, and other Protestant traditions. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism** (often called the Great Schism) | 1054 CE | Same event as #1 – the formal division between the Western (Roman Catholic) and Eastern (Orthodox) branches of Christianity. |

These three events are commonly referred to as the “great schisms” in Christian history.
